passages.label: A
passages.text: A tape measure gives one part of Sultan Kösen's story. He lives in Türkiye, a country between Europe and Asia, and he was born near Mardin, an old city in the south-east. His date of birth is 10 December 1982. Guinness World Records made his height known across the globe.

passages.label: B
passages.text: Kösen’s family members are all an ordinary height, and he has three brothers and one sister. His own growth changed when he was about ten, and he became much taller than the people around him. Later, doctors found the health problem that made him grow so quickly.

passages.label: C
passages.text: Because of his height, Kösen could not finish school and took a job as a farmer to support his family. His long reach helps when he works around the house, where he can hang curtains without a ladder. Many ordinary tools are designed for someone of normal height, so his size can also make daily work more difficult.

passages.label: D
passages.text: In 2009, Guinness World Records measured Kösen at 246.5 centimetres, then recorded 251 centimetres in 2011. A writer can report those measurements as the headline. A teacher might ask a student to compare the lengths with a doorway, because a very tall son or daughter can face a design limit that few people notice.

passages.label: E
passages.text: Finding clothes, shoes and beds that fit takes Kösen extra time and money. An engineer might design furniture for an unusually tall customer, while a doctor treated Kösen’s condition in the United States and stopped his growth. A father or mother may want to listen to his description of everyday life as well as learning the record.

passages.label: F
passages.text: Kösen is interested in music, and watching television is a hobby he can enjoy at home. In 2013, his wedding to Merve Dibo took place in Mardin, and many guests joined the celebration. His unusual height explains why people across the globe recognise him, and details of his home life show what this farmer and traveller enjoys doing.
